This Fully Bespoke Camper Van Is a Luxurious Mobile Home With Plenty of Ingenious Features
20 photos
Photo: Vanboerse/ YouTube screenshot
Most travelers and aspiring vanlifers are looking for a personalized experience, so a custom camper van conversion tailored specifically to their needs and tastes is the way to go. For many customers, this means a unique layout, hand-picked finishes, and special features meant to make their life on the road easier and more pleasant.
Camper Schmiede, a premium camper van manufacturer based in Germany’s Lower Rhine region, takes this approach to heart, offering their customers the opportunity to create true dream campers. Instead of standard layouts and fixed features, the company works closely with each client to develop unique conversions around their specific requirements.
With a focus on high-quality materials, first-class craftsmanship, and attention to detail, the team builds rigs that feel clearly different from the mass-produced ones. The camper van featured here is one of Camper Schmiede’s latest creations, a fully bespoke MAN TGE conversion with an ingenious bathroom, a home cinema system, and an elevator bed.
Built on a brand-new MAN TGE equipped with a 177-hp engine and an eight-speed automatic transmission, this camper van measures 6.8 meters (22.3 feet) long and 2.8 meters (9.2 feet) tall, providing just enough interior space to create a comfortable mobile habitat.
Photo: Vanboerse/ YouTube screenshot Finished in Indium Gray Metallic, its exterior combines ruggedness with elegance. The team adorned it with several customer-requested features, such as a front light bar and rugged rear-mounted carriers from Overland Equipment, providing space for storage boxes, a spare tire, and additional gear. On top of the van, there is a large roof rack with a rooftop terrace and walkable solar panels.
Built using a lightweight aluminum honeycomb system, the roof terrace is a great addition for outdoor lovers, offering an additional space to hang out. A full-length awning is also installed on the side, providing a shade area at camp. As such, owners have two options for enjoying the outdoors: relax next to the camper or head up to the roof with a cup of coffee and a different view of their surroundings.
Designed for anything from weekend escapes to full-time van living , the interior is warm and functional, with custom-made furniture and a layout designed to ensure everyday comfort. Camper Schmiede efficiently used the available space, squeezing in a generous lounge, a fully equipped kitchen, an ingenious bathroom/closet system, and a proper bed that descends from the ceiling.
Photo: Vanboerse/ YouTube screenshot One of the highlights inside this custom van is the inventive rotating closet and shower system that allows for flexible space utilization. On the outside, the 2-in-1 system features regular doors revealing storage, but another handle reveals this is a rotating module where the closets are built directly in the path of the wet bath door. When you open the bathroom door to use the shower, the closet effectively slides out of the wet bath, revealing a full-height, isolated shower stall.
The bathroom itself includes a water-saving recirculating shower that captures, filters, sterilizes, and reuses shower water in a closed loop, making it possible to enjoy luxurious hot showers off-grid. A vanity counter with a small sink and a Clesana X1 portable, heat-sealing toilet tucked away in a dedicated compartment are also included.
There is a second, larger wardrobe next to the bathroom, providing more space for clothes and personal belongings, as well as a narrow heated compartment with an air vent, designed to dry damp clothes or equipment.
Photo: Vanboerse/ YouTube screenshot Like in most camper conversions , the kitchen stretches along one side of the van and features custom cabinetry in dark gray and a wood-toned solid countertop. In terms of cooking equipment, the customer opted for an undermount sink with a cutting board insert, an integrated cooktop, an oven, and a refrigerator.
What makes this van different from other conversions is that both the cooktop and the oven run on diesel, as does the integrated hydronic underfloor heating system. And since diesel is the primary energy source, the owner won’t have to carry gas cylinders or rely fully on battery energy for cooking and heating.
The cabinetry and countertop run the entire length of the van, with an angular shape in the lounge area to facilitate easy circulation. It gradually narrows toward the rear and then transforms into a nice shelving unit that completes the lounge area.
Photo: Vanboerse/ YouTube screenshot Speaking of the lounge, instead of two opposing benches, the client opted for a large L-shaped built-in sofa with comfortable seating for four. It is accompanied by an adjustable table for dining/working functionality, while a projector and screen turn the space into a home theater. The projector attaches magnetically to the underside of the elevator bed, so you can easily remove it if you want to use it outside, for instance.
When it’s time for sleep, the bed drops down from the ceiling at the push of a button. It’s a full-fledged longitudinal bed measuring 2 by 1.45 meters (6.6 by 4.8 feet) and comes with a Gisamed premium folding mattress. There is also a skylight from Outbound above the bed for stargazing.
Up front in the driver’s cabin, Camper Schmiede swapped out the original driver and passenger seats for custom Scheel-Mann seats for an extra level of comfort. They both swivel to face the living space and offer extra seating. Above the cab, an enclosed compartment offers a generous amount of storage space, while a narrow shelf behind the driver’s seat could easily be used as a nice space to work on your laptop, though the rear lounge would be much more comfortable for remote work.
Photo: Vanboerse/ YouTube screenshot Designed for self-sufficient travel, this MAN GTE camper van is equipped with 350 watts of solar panels on the roof and a Victron electrical system to manage the onboard power. Both the fresh-water and gray-water tanks are mounted underneath the vehicle, freeing up valuable interior storage space. Each tank holds approximately 150 liters (40 gallons), which the builder says would be enough for about a week, with the recirculating shower really boosting the “self-sufficiency” factor.
This particular van conversion is not equipped with one, but Camper Schmiede offers an optional feature called the Soul Floater. It’s an ergonomic, fold-out lounger that attaches to the rear of the vehicle and accommodates two adults, with a maximum load capacity of 200 kg (441 lbs).
Since this is a fully custom build , no pricing information is available, but Camper Schmiede’s conversions typically hover around the €269,000 mark, which is approximately $299,500 at the current exchange rate.
